A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material across the reordered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging, singular-vector alignment and model-width experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds layer-input projection analyses in Appendix E and Figures 10–12.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same Sinkhorn-based WM and STE objectives, permutation searches and model-merging procedures. Appendix E adds analysis without changing these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-classification datasets and model-merging scenarios. The new activation analyses use the existing MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 coverage.

E2.justification: The WM-versus-STE comparisons and controls without permutation remain unchanged. The added projection analyses introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces test-set measurements of expected squared projections of layer inputs onto right singular vectors, including measurements across model widths. Existing training settings, merging ratios and benchmark evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially extends the mechanism analysis by testing whether dominant right singular vectors align with actual layer inputs and how this relationship depends on width. Figures 10–12 complement v1's analyses of weight spectra and alignment between models.

E5.justification: The existing mean-and-standard-deviation summaries and run-count statements are retained. The new projection plots use the same ten-seed curve-display practice already used for singular spectra, without introducing a different uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–9 retain their results. Figures 10–12 add substantial mechanistic findings: intermediate-layer input projections concentrate on leading singular directions, with stronger concentration in wider CNNs. These are additional findings rather than improved benchmark performance.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a Lipschitz/Jensen bound on expected layer-output differences, an aligned-input example and a truncation argument. v3 also corrects Fourier conjugation in the convolutional SVD derivation and restores the missing normalization in the appendix theorem bounding R; the main-text definition of R is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, stated contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: distance reduction alone does not explain LMC, WM aligns dominant singular vectors, and WM has advantages over STE when merging three or more models.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds an input-distribution-dependent explanation of why layer outputs can remain close despite large weight distances, and connects model width to concentration along dominant singular directions. The original limitations are retained, moving from Appendix E to F.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix C becomes v3 Appendix B with the same architecture details, learning rates, search budgets, BatchNorm repair, hardware and implementation-repository information. No implementation or resource-access change is documented.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion are unchanged. The added analysis does not introduce citations or revise the paper's positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 moves experimental setup and supplementary results ahead of the proofs, corrects the placement of Section 3.2, adds Appendix E and updates cross-references. Existing prose and the main narrative are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figures 10–12 substantially expand the visual evidence with layerwise projection plots and grids comparing model widths. Figures 1 and 6 receive new color palettes, while Table 3 and Figures 6–9 move with the appendix reorganization.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the central explanation by directly examining layer-input projections, which v1's weight-only analyses left implicit, and corrects existing mathematical inconsistencies. The gain is limited: Appendix E remains conditional and contains algebraic slips in its trace expansion and distance formula. Its evidence improves support for the mechanism without fully establishing it.
